value.title: Git AI as the telemetry collector — v1

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Harness stops collecting its own telemetry and hands AI-attribution collection to git-ai (Apache-2.0, github.com/git-ai-project/git-ai). v1 DISABLES harness capture by default rather than removing it — the kill switch and its three enforcement points already exist, and the read path is deliberately ungated so the 123 existing refs/harness-telemetry/* stay queryable. The build is harness doctor: detect git-ai, install it from a pinned version+SHA manifest via our own cross-platform download-and-verify (never their install.sh), install the agent hooks on our own terms, and re-check later when a new coding harness appears. Doing our own download is what makes prime's trace2-consent condition possible at all — their installer calls install-hooks itself and would seize trace2 before we could ask. No semantic or flow capture in v1; fleet lineage goes dark until v2.

sections.name: goals
value: Harness telemetry capture is off by default at ship, with the read path untouched — existing published refs stay queryable
git-ai is installed only from a pinned version + per-platform SHA-256, verified before anything is placed on disk
The download and verification path is cross-platform with no shelling out — Node stdlib fetch + crypto, one code path
A version bump is a one-file diff, produced by a regenerate command, never by the install path re-pinning itself
harness doctor owns the collector lifecycle: install, hook installation, and later re-check when a new coding harness appears
Doctor reports collection health from an observed recent checkpoint, not from daemon liveness
The destructive machine-wide trace2 change is never silent — snapshot, report, consent, and record even when empty

sections.name: non_goals
value: Removing or deleting harness telemetry code — v1 disables, so v2 can migrate rather than rebuild
Any semantic or flow capture (gates, findings, chores, phases, agent/human time) — explicitly out of scope for v1
Fleet lineage (pij seat identity, subagent parentage) — goes dark until v2, ruled and accepted
Redistributing or bundling the git-ai binary — we fetch and verify their published artifact, we do not ship it
Reading or publishing git-ai's richer local data, or emitting an adjacent harness notes ref — both are v2

value.claim: A shipped harness collects no telemetry: capture, publish and housekeeping are all no-ops with no environment variable set, proven by asserting each of the three existing enforcement points short-circuits on a default install.
The telemetry READ path is unaffected: `telemetry pull` and `telemetry report` still succeed against an existing published ref after capture is disabled.
`harness doctor` installs git-ai only from the committed pin manifest — a version tag plus one SHA-256 per platform artifact — and never resolves 'latest'.
The downloaded artifact is hashed and compared BEFORE it is placed at its final path; verification happens on a temp file.
A SHA-256 mismatch installs nothing, leaves no partial file, and reports an error naming the expected and actual digests.
Platform resolution covers all six published artifacts (macos/linux/windows × x64/arm64) and performs hashing via Node's crypto module, with no shell-out to shasum/sha256sum/certutil.
git-ai's auto-updater is disabled — `disable_auto_updates` and `disable_version_checks` are written to its config BEFORE the binary is first run, so the pin cannot drift on its own.

Before EVERY `install-hooks` invocation — first install and every later re-check — doctor reads the global trace2 config. If it is NON-EMPTY, doctor does NOT invoke `install-hooks` at all: it warns that git-ai telemetry could not be installed because trace2 is present, names what is there, and prints manual instructions. If it is EMPTY, doctor records that it was observed empty and proceeds. Doctor never destroys a trace2 config, so no consent mechanism is required.

Doctor never invokes git-ai's `install.sh`, so no shell rc, PATH entry, or binary symlink is modified by us. It DOES bound and disclose what `install-hooks` still changes on its own: a global trace2 reset, a daemon restart, reformatting of each detected agent's config file, and — because git-ai runs `uninstall_skills` whenever `--skills` is absent — removal of git-ai skill links on every invocation.

Doctor reports a SIMPLE, bounded health read: pinned binary present and hash-matching, agent hooks current, daemon process reachable, and the note schema version as expected. It does NOT claim to prove that collection is actually occurring — see ac-0012.
'Could not determine' is a distinct reported state — it is never rendered as healthy, and never folded into 'no data'.
Doctor warns and never blocks: no doctor verdict causes a non-zero exit that halts a developer mid-flight.
The pin is data, not code: changing the pinned version and its hashes is a single-file diff requiring no source change.
A regenerate command fetches every platform artifact for a given version and rewrites the manifest; the install path never writes the manifest.
The expected note schema version (`authorship/3.0.0`) is pinned in the same manifest and asserted after install, so binary drift and format drift are reviewed together.

Re-running doctor after a new coding harness is installed on the machine detects that its hooks are missing and reports it. Doctor does NOT automatically re-invoke install-hooks to fix it: once a first install has succeeded, git-ai's own trace2 keys are present, and harness cannot establish from a key name plus a local record that those keys are still the ones it wrote rather than a value the operator has since set. Observed-empty trace2 remains the SOLE automatic path. A re-check that finds any existing trace2 reports the unhooked agent and prints manual instructions, exactly as a first install does.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, deliberately deferred past v1: there is no reliable signal today that proves the capture chain is intact. `git ai status --json` reports only the CURRENT uncommitted working log, which git-ai deletes at commit, and its `time_ago` is a human string rather than a timestamp — so a healthy collector reads empty immediately after any commit. v1 must record this gap explicitly rather than ship a check that cannot distinguish a broken collector from a clean tree.
Installing the git-ai CLI is INDEPENDENT of installing hooks: a trace2 block prevents hook installation only, and never fails, reverts, or skips the pinned binary install.
Doctor reports 'CLI installed, hooks not installed (trace2 present)' as its own distinct state — not as healthy, not as a failed install, and not as 'could not determine'.

The download path handles every failure mode explicitly, not just digest mismatch: non-2xx HTTP, redirects, connect/read timeout, and an interrupted or short write each abort the install, remove the temp file, and report the cause.

The placed binary is executable on Unix (mode set explicitly after verification) and replaces any existing binary atomically, so an interrupted upgrade never leaves a half-written or non-executable git-ai in place.
An unsupported platform/arch combination is reported as unsupported and installs nothing, rather than falling back to a default artifact.
Manifest regeneration is all-or-nothing: if any one of the six artifacts fails to fetch or hash, the existing manifest is left untouched.
Flipping the capture default is proven at all three enforcement points — capture, publish and housekeeping each assert a no-op on a default install, not just the one that reads the setting.
Bumping the pinned version is proven to be a single-file change: a test asserts no source file outside the manifest needs editing to move versions.
